findings.description: SYS-SUP-033 relies on SYS-SUP-051 to select the reported state, but OP-SYS-015 records that the state during fault handling, for a start-up fault, and after a code 8 report is undecided. The expected status response is therefore not established for those histories.
findings.requested_change: Resolve OP-SYS-015 and specify the state selection so the expected GET STATUS response is uniquely verifiable.

findings.description: CON-SUP-107 and CON-SUP-124 specify the CRC polynomial but not the initial value, input and output reflection, final XOR, or stored-reference byte order. The expected comparison result for a given image and reference is not unique.
findings.requested_change: Resolve OP-SYS-014 and specify the CRC parameters and reference byte order needed to determine the start-up comparison result.

findings.description: The run-time CRC comparison lacks the initial value, input and output reflection, final XOR, and reference byte order. CON-SUP-124 identifies the polynomial and reference location but does not determine a unique comparison result.
findings.requested_change: Resolve OP-SYS-014 and specify the CRC parameters and reference byte order needed to determine the run-time comparison result.

findings.description: CON-SUP-125 lists state labels without transition rules. SYS-SUP-051 selects STARTUP or OPERATIONAL between fault detection and safe-state entry, including during a start-up fault and after a code 8 report, although OP-SYS-015 identifies these cases as undecided.
findings.requested_change: Resolve OP-SYS-015 and align the state-selection conditions with the product decision.

findings.description: The configuration integrity comparison specifies only the CRC polynomial. OP-SYS-014 records missing CRC parameters and stored CRC byte order, so the expected result for a given configuration block and reference cannot yet be determined.
findings.requested_change: Resolve OP-SYS-014 and specify the CRC parameters and stored CRC byte order needed to verify the configuration integrity comparison.

findings.description: CON-SUP-110 calls for consecutive supervisor resets with the same fault code, interpreted by CON-SUP-117 as latching on the third detection. SYS-SUP-028 requires three detections of the same code without 60 seconds of fault-free operation but does not exclude an intervening detection and reset for a different code, so it can latch where the consecutive condition is not met.
findings.requested_change: Clarify the treatment of intervening fault codes against CON-SUP-110 and CON-SUP-117, and state the resulting latch condition consistently.
